Protect Yourself & Your Family from Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Recognize the Signs and Symptoms of Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning Loss of consciousnessHeadache DizzinessShortness of breath Nausea or vomiting Chest pain Collapse Remember… Carbon Monoxide ( CO) Poisoning DANGER! Carbon monoxide (CO) is an odorless, colorless gas that kills without warning. It claims the lives of hundreds of people every year and makes thousands more ill. Many household items including gas- and oil-burning furnaces, portable generators, and charcoal grills produce this poison gas. Following these important steps can keep your family safe. CO DETECTORS • Install battery-operated or battery back-up CO detectors near every sleeping area in your home. • Check CO detectors regularly to be sure they are functioning properly. OIL & GAS FURNACES • Have your furnace inspected every year. PORTABLE GENERATORS • Never use a generator inside your home or garage, even if doors and windows are open. • Only use generators outside, more than 20 feet away from your home, doors, and windows. PROTECT YOUR FAMILY If you live in a home with gas, oil or coal burning appliances, check your CO alarms or CO detectors regularly to be sure they are functioning properly.

CS283134-D August 29, 2017 National Center for Environmental Health Division of Environmental Hazards and Health Effects Prevention Guidelines: You Can Prevent Carbon Monoxide Exposure z DO have your heating system, water heater and any other gas, oil, or coal burning appliances serviced by a qualified technician every year. z DO install a battery-operated CO detector in your home and check or replace the battery when you change the time on your clocks each spring and fall. If the detector sounds, leave your home immediately and call 911. z DO seek prompt medical attention if you suspect CO poisoning and are feeling dizzy, light-headed, or nauseous. z DON’T use a generator, charcoal grill, camp stove, or other gasoline or charcoal-burning device inside your home, basement, or garage or near a window. z DON’T run a car or truck inside a garage attached to your house, even if you leave the door open. z DON’T burn anything in a stove or fireplace that isn’t vented. z DON’T heat your house with a gas oven. z DON’T use a generator, pressure washer, or any gasoline-powered engine less than 20 feet from any window, door, or vent. Use an extension cord that is more than 20 feet long to keep the generator at a safe distance.
